children: New Delhi, Oct. 5 -- Looking for one mutual fund scheme that covers almost the entire Indian equity market, including micro caps? Nifty Total Market Index funds offer investors a passive route to large-, mid-, small-, and micro-cap stocks within a single portfolio.

The Nifty Total Market Index tracks 750 stocks and includes all stocks that are part of the Nifty 500 and Nifty Microcap 250 indices. This gives investors exposure to large-, mid-, and small-cap companies that dominate traditional mutual fund categories, along with micro-cap stocks.
Since Nifty Total Market Index funds are relatively new, their fund-level performance history is limited. However, the historical performance of the underlying benchmark provides some context.

The broader market exposure has also translated into relatively better performance than the Nifty 50 over several periods. The Nifty Total Market TRI has fallen by 3.14% over the last 1 year, compared with a decline of 8.74% for the Nifty 50 TRI.

Over three years, the Nifty Total Market TRI has delivered 9.49%, compared with 5.75% for the Nifty 50. Its five-year return stands at 9.28%, against 6.29% for the Nifty 50, while the 10-year return is 12.87%, compared with 11.38%.
The total market index has also remained ahead of the Nifty 500 TRI, the benchmark for flexi-cap funds, which invest across large-, mid-, and small-cap stocks.
However, these are index TRI (Total Return Index) returns, which include both capital gains and dividends from the underlying stocks.
Nifty Total Market Index funds seek to replicate the performance of the underlying index, but actual scheme returns can differ because of factors such as expenses and tracking error.
Their one-year returns are currently in a relatively narrow range, with Mirae Asset at -3.44%, Groww at -3.66%, Bandhan at -3.71%, and Angel One at -3.41%.
However, a meaningful long-term performance comparison at the fund level is not yet available.

For investors seeking broad equity exposure through a single passive fund, the category offers an alternative to combining multiple market-cap-specific funds. However, its performance will continue to depend on how the different segments of the Indian equity market perform.
